findings.summary: Toggle-off now emits a Yorkie `removeStyleByPath` op on the hottest editing path (B/I/U/S); if Yorkie history cannot reverse TreeStyleRemove, Cmd+Z after a toggle-off silently stops restoring the flag
findings.evidence: With the demotion in `Doc.styleOffAsClear`, every B/I/U/S off-toggle now reaches `YorkieDocStore.applyStyleInTree` with the key set to `undefined`, so `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163) returns the attr and `tree.removeStyleByPath(...)` runs at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1881 — previously only `styleByPath` ran for a toggle-off (the `false` was serialized), and `removeStyleByPath` was reached only by the rare removeLink / clear-formatting paths. Docs undo is Yorkie-history based (`this.doc.history.undo()` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2611), so the reversibility of the removeStyle op is now load-bearing for the most common formatting action in the product. I could not verify the SDK's reverse-op support from this checkout (the Yorkie SDK is not installed in node_modules here); confirming needs a collab/integration run that toggles bold off and then undoes it against a real Yorkie doc. Fix, if real, belongs in the Yorkie store (emit a compensating style write) rather than in the new Doc code.

findings.summary: The mixed-key branch of `styleOffAsClear` (one style object containing both a style-supplied key and a non-supplied key) is never exercised, though the test comment claims it is
findings.evidence: In 'keeps an explicit false where the named style supplies the flag' (document.test.ts:345-367) the comment at line 360 says "A key the style does not supply is still cleared **in the same write**", but the test issues two *separate* `applyInlineStyle` calls: `{ italic: false }` then `{ bold: false }`. The interesting branch in `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:405-417) is the copy-on-write path `cleared = cleared ?? { ...style }` combined with `if (defaults[key]) continue`, i.e. a single patch like `{ italic: false, bold: false }` on a Heading 6 where `italic:false` must survive while `bold` is deleted. A regression that built `cleared` as `{}` instead of a spread of `style`, or that cleared/kept the wrong key when both are present, would drop the italic override and no test in the diff or elsewhere would fail. I grepped packages/docs/test for combined boolean-off patches and found none.

findings.summary: New cross-cutting storage invariant is recorded only in docs/tasks/*, not in any design doc
findings.evidence: The change establishes a model-level invariant — "a boolean inline key turned off is *cleared*, not stored as `false`, except where the block's named style supplies it truthy" — plus a new merge semantic in `block-helpers.applyInlineStyle` (a patch key set to `undefined` deletes the key). Both are consumed across packages (docs engine, slides text-box editor, `YorkieDocStore.removedInlineStyleAttrs`) and interact with the named-style lazy cascade. No `docs/design/**` file was touched by the diff; the only written record is `docs/tasks/active/20260819-docs-inline-style-off-clears-key-{todo,lessons}.md`. CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 and :58-60 require writing/updating a design doc under `docs/design/<area>/` for a non-trivial change, folding into the canonical doc. The natural homes are `docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md` §"Clear formatting" (which documents the `undefined`-means-remove convention at :229-242 but says nothing about the boolean toggles) and `docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md` §"Cascade resolution model" (:117-131, where the false-pins-against-redefinition hazard lives).
